queue_order.move: 7369D0/5B1C70 appends chosen record to destination by value, swaps chosen source slot with final record through a1C0-byte stack copy, then decrements sourceend. contact_iteration.prepare: 738A20/5B3E20 copies inverse inertia and computes r=point-bodyPosition for each present body. Local point velocity is linearVelocity+angularVelocity cross r. Stores(A-B) dot normal inC. Nonzero friction builds tangents, stores relative tangent velocities in10/14 and adds .5*delta*body10 to those tangent terms only when delta>0. Normal term does not receive that delta contribution.
contact_iteration.mode2: Preparation subtracts penetration/control from normal velocity when mode==2. Component resolver subsequently clears1B4/1B8. The only direct caller734200 supplies mode2, so penetration is handled through a velocity bias and the separate position loop is skipped.
contact_iteration.selection: For at most4*contactCount iterations, choose strict lowest(1+restitution)*normalVelocity below-negative velocityThreshold. Ordinary ties preserve earlier scanned contact. If none qualifies, stop.73A1C0 applies requested change velocityThreshold-selectedScore. Propagate each returned deltaLinear+deltaAngular cross each other contact lever arm into its normal/tangent velocities: add for itsA, subtract for itsB. Only shared nonnull body pointers participate.
contact_iteration.position_loop: For modes otherthan2, an additional at-most4*N loop chooses maximum penetration above positionThreshold and calls73ACC0 with penetration-positionThreshold*.5. Propagates corrections into contactE4 using body matches. Mode0 divides correction across inverse mass and angular contributions, caps angular share at.1*|r projected perpendicular to normal|, transfers excess to linear share, updates position and quaternion. Other modes use linear inverse-mass weighting only. Exact mode0 quaternion angle arithmetic is not fully modeled; no located direct scene path selects it.

impulse_contract.friction_zero: 7390D0 forms scalar K=sum overpresentbodies[1/m+(r cross n) dot Iinverse*(r cross n)].73A1C0 computesj=request/K, applies +j*n/m and +Iinverse*(r cross n)*j toA, opposite signs toB. Updates body velocities via setters and returns requested changes for propagation. Angular setter can reject nonfinite values; returned deltas are still used by outer propagation. No local guard for zero mass or singularK.
impulse_contract.friction_matrix: For friction!=0, use basis(n,t1,t2). Matrix K_ab=sum[dot(r cross basis_a,Iinverse*(r cross basis_b))]+inverseMassSum ondiagonal. Separate one-body and two-body implementations populate symmetric fields18..38 and angular caches; equivalence assumes valid symmetric inertia input. Factorization writesL10=M10/M00,D1=M11-M10*L10,L20=M20/M00,L21=(M21-M10*L20)/D1,D2=M22-M20*L20-(M21-M10*L20)*L21.
impulse_contract.friction_solve: Solve three contact-space impulse components for(requestedNormalChange,-tangentV1,-tangentV2) using those factors. If tangential magnitude>friction*normalImpulse, recompute normal with sliding direction held and scale tangents to friction*normal; if that recomputed normal isnegative, zero tangents and recompute restitution-only normal. Convert by n/t1/t2 to world impulse and apply to bodies.
impulse_contract.single_body_caveat: The nonzero-friction exactly-one-body path chooses A orB caches and applies a positive worldImpulse/m to whichever body is present; unlike the both-body and zero-friction paths, there is no explicit B-only sign inversion. Reviewed assembly confirms this branch. Caller shape/body ordering and reachability remain open; do not silently replace it with an assumed symmetric textbook implementation.
impulse_contract.caches: First73A1C0 call builds response matrix and sets both contact1B4/1B8=1. Further iterations reuse it. Body velocities change but body positions do not in scene mode2. Contact/body fields atsame numeric offset are separate objects.
impulse_contract.basis: 7403D0 chooses t1=(0,-nz,ny)/sqrt(ny²+nz²) when|nx|<=|ny|, otherwise(nz,0,-nx)/sqrt(nx²+nz²). t2=n cross t1. No zero-normal guard.
